about: Static example of the plain-language generator: the faculty description below and the case it produces. Loaded without calling Bedrock, so the demo works offline. Clinical content is a draft for faculty review. Built around 'Rubric for Pediatric Treatment.docx' (SPLP 6510, Pediatric Hearing Treatment, Session 1).

request.text:
A 10-year-old girl in 5th grade comes with her mother for her first aural rehabilitation session. Her hearing loss was found at age 4 after she failed a school hearing screening. She wears behind-the-ear hearing aids in both ears but often takes them off at recess because other children tease her. She notices ringing in her ears when it is quiet at night. She has an IEP and sits near the front of the class, but struggles to follow group discussions. Her biggest goal is to understand her friends in the noisy cafeteria at lunch. She is shy at first and warms up with encouragement; her mother has many questions.

She is 10 years old, female. Main concern: Bilateral moderately-severe sensorineural hearing loss; first aural rehabilitation session with a speech-language pathologist.

Audiogram: bilateral moderately-severe sensorineural hearing loss. Pure-tone average right 60 dB HL, left 65 dB HL. Aided thresholds 25-30 dB HL from 500-4000 Hz.

Learning objectives:
- Introduce yourself and your role in a professional, empathetic way
- Complete a needs assessment: age at diagnosis, device use, other auditory complaints, educational needs, and the most important communication challenge today
- Review the audiogram and explain the severity of the hearing loss sensitively, using the Speech Banana
- Set realistic expectations: audiologist vs SLP, what aural rehabilitation is, and answer questions

case.name: Maya Torres
case.summary: 10-year-old with bilateral hearing loss · first aural rehabilitation session (with her mother)
case.background: Fifth grader who lives with her mother and younger brother. Likes drawing and soccer.
case.persona: Shy at first, warms up with encouragement
case.behavior: Maya is shy and gives short answers at first. She avoids talking about teasing or her feelings about her hearing aids until the student is warm and patient; her mother sometimes answers for her.

facts.label: Presenting case
facts.record: 10-year-old with bilateral moderately-severe sensorineural hearing loss attending her first aural rehabilitation session, accompanied by her mother.
facts.patient_text: Hi. I'm Maya. My mom said we're here to talk about my hearing.

facts.label: Age at diagnosis
facts.record: Hearing loss identified at age 4 after a failed school hearing screening.
facts.patient_text: I found out when I was 4. I didn't pass the hearing test at school.

facts.label: Device use
facts.record: Bilateral behind-the-ear hearing aids. Removes them at recess because of teasing.
facts.patient_text: I have hearing aids in both ears. Sometimes I take them out at recess because some kids make fun of them.

facts.label: Other auditory complaints
facts.record: Reports tinnitus (ringing) when it is quiet at night. Hyperacusis not reported.
facts.patient_text: When it's really quiet at night I hear a ringing sound. Loud sounds don't really bother me.

facts.label: Educational needs
facts.record: 5th grade with an IEP and preferential seating. Difficulty following group discussions.
facts.patient_text: I'm in fifth grade. I sit up front and my teacher helps, but when everyone talks at once in groups I get lost.

facts.label: Most important communication challenge
facts.record: Primary goal: understanding friends in the noisy school cafeteria.
facts.patient_text: Lunch is the hardest. It's so loud in the cafeteria and I can't understand my friends, so I just nod.
keywords: what would you like to work on

facts.label: Feelings about hearing aids
facts.record: Feels embarrassed when peers notice her hearing aids.
facts.patient_text: I don't like it when people notice my hearing aids. It's kind of embarrassing.

facts.label: Caregiver questions
facts.record: Mother asks whether the hearing loss will get worse and whether therapy will help.
facts.patient_text: My mom wants to know if my hearing will get worse, and if this will actually help me.
keywords: what would you like to know

facts.label: Audiogram
facts.record: Bilateral moderately-severe sensorineural hearing loss. Pure-tone average right 60 dB HL, left 65 dB HL. Aided thresholds 25-30 dB HL from 500-4000 Hz.
facts.patient_text: My mom has my hearing test paper. It shows both of my ears.

facts.label: Teaching note
facts.record: Expected: explain severity sensitively with the Speech Banana. Unaided, soft high-frequency sounds (s, f, th) fall below her thresholds; aided, most speech sounds are audible. Distinguish the audiologist (testing, fitting devices) from the SLP (listening and communication therapy).

objectives.label: Ask about age at diagnosis and device use
objectives.suggestion: Ask when the hearing loss was found and how she uses her hearing aids day to day.

objectives.label: Ask about other auditory complaints
objectives.suggestion: Ask about ringing (tinnitus) or sensitivity to loud sounds (hyperacusis).

objectives.label: Explore educational needs
objectives.suggestion: Ask about school, classroom support, and where listening is hardest.

objectives.label: Identify the most important communication challenge
objectives.suggestion: Ask what she most wants to be able to do. Her answer sets the therapy goal.

objectives.label: Review the audiogram
objectives.suggestion: Look at the audiogram together and explain what it means in child-friendly words.

objectives.label: Acknowledge feelings and answer caregiver questions
objectives.suggestion: Ask how she feels about her hearing aids, and invite her mother's questions.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Introduces self as the speech-language pathologist and explains the session
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Start by introducing yourself, your role, and what today's session will cover.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Uses empathetic, child-friendly language about the hearing aids and teasing
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Acknowledge how the teasing feels before moving on.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Explains the severity of the hearing loss sensitively in plain language
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Explain what moderately-severe hearing loss means in words a 10-year-old understands.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Uses the Speech Banana to show what she hears with and without hearing aids
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Use the Speech Banana to compare what she hears with and without her hearing aids.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Explains the difference between an audiologist and an SLP
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Explain that the audiologist tests hearing and fits devices, and the SLP works on listening and communication.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Explains what aural rehabilitation is and how it can help
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Describe aural rehabilitation and how it connects to her lunchroom goal.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Sets realistic expectations (hearing aids help but do not restore typical hearing)
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Set realistic expectations: devices and therapy help but do not restore typical hearing.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Invites and answers the child's and mother's questions
cues: what would you like to know
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Invite questions from both Maya and her mother.

scoring_criteria.criterion: Builds trust before asking about feelings and teasing (guarded patient)
scoring_criteria.feedback_if_missed: Maya is guarded: slow down and build trust before asking about teasing or feelings.

reports.title: Audiology report (synthetic)
reports.body:
AUDIOLOGY REPORT - SYNTHETIC CASE FOR EDUCATION
Patient: Maya Torres, 10 years
Reason: annual hearing aid check

Pure-tone audiometry: bilateral moderately-severe sensorineural hearing loss.
Pure-tone average: right 60 dB HL, left 65 dB HL.
Aided thresholds (bilateral BTE hearing aids): 25-30 dB HL from 500-4000 Hz.
Tympanometry: normal middle-ear function, both ears.

Plan: continue bilateral amplification; refer to speech-language pathology for aural rehabilitation.
